title: Il Lombardia 2026: Our form guide

Il Lombardia 2026: Our form guide

The final Monument of the season is here. Il Lombardia takes place on Saturday and five-time reigning champion Tadej Pogačar will not be there, providing a massive opportunity for someone else to grab a Monument victory.

A pair of former Monument winners will line up at the start in Remco Evenepoel and Primož Roglič, however the favourite for the title is Pogačar’s young teammate Isaac del Toro, and French prodigy Paul Seixas is a threat to all of them.

Below, we’ll assess the form of the favourites to win the Race of the Falling Leaves.

Remco Evenepoel (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe)

Not even a crash can keep Remco Evenepoel down. The Belgian stormed to victory in the road race at the European Championships against Giulio Ciccone despite hitting the ground with 36km to go and could well claim his first Monument since 2023 at Il Lombardia.

The Belgian has had two consecutive second places at Il Lombardia against Pogačar. and he’s just claimed one of the Slovenian’s titles in his absence – will he get another this weekend?

Isaac del Toro (UAE Team Emirates XRG)

Il Lombardia has been the most successful Monument for Isaac del Toro in his young career so far, the 22-year-old racing to fifth behind teammate Pogačar last year. After his mightily impressive third place in the Tour de France and overall victory in the Lidl Deutschland Tour, Del Toro has been placing highly in the one-day races in the back half of the season. He won the GP Montréal, raced to sixth in the World Championship time-trial and fifth in the road race. He launched an attack at the recent Gran Piemonte but it couldn’t stick and he ended up 82nd.

UAE Team Emirates XRG bring a strong squad to Lombardia with recently crowned World Champion Brandon McNulty too. He likely won’t be able to slip away though with those rainbow bands on.

Paul Seixas (Decathlon CMA CGM)

Carrying the French flag Paul Seixas, who has hopefully recovered mentally from his post-Worlds self-deprecation when he chastised himself for cramping in the final few kilometres of the road race, where he finished 15th.

The Frenchman won the junior men’s Liège-Bastogne-Liège in 2024 and has been a force to be reckoned with since stepping up to the WorldTour level. In the last edition of Il Lombardia, he raced to seventh place on debut. This season, he has taken a massive step up and was notably best of the rest behind Pogačar in Strade Bianche and Liège-Bastogne-Liège. Now, there’s no Pogačar on the start line…

Tom Pidcock (Pinarello Q36.5)

Second has been the name of the game as of late for Pinarello 36.5’s Tom Pidcock. The Brit finished behind Davide Piganzoli at the Giro dell’Emilia and Jarno Widar at Tre Valli Varesine. His wins this season have mostly come either from winning a small group sprint or launching a solo attack, and the parcours at Il Lombardia suits him. He was certainly one of the strongest at Worlds, and has a great shot at claiming his first Monument.

Giulio Ciccone (Lidl-Trek)

Another man that knows a lot about almost, Giulio Ciccone has had a slew of second places this year including at the recent European Championships. The Italian launched his sprint against Evenepoel and almost won but was defeated by the tightest of photofinishes. He suffered a similar fate at the Vuelta a Burgos when beaten by Oscar Onley, and again by Evenepoel at the GP Québec.

Ciccone is yet to record a win this season out of mountains classifications and this is set to be his final race for Lidl-Trek. Victory in a Monument would be a welcome goodbye gift. He is clearly in form and has previously podiumed at Il Lombardia with a third place in 2024.

Lidl-Trek also bring another strong option in Quinn Simmons. The American has notched fourth place in his last three races finished in the GP Montréal, World Championshipa Road Race and Tre Valli Varesine, and will almost certainly be on the offensive again here.

Ben Healy (EF Education-EasyPost)

Ben Healy has had a couple of top ten finishes lately in the GP Montréal, World Championship Road Race and Giro dell’Emilia, however he is uncharacteristically yet to notch a win in 2026. That’s not for a lack of trying. He’s been involved in plenty a breakaway throughout the year, notably at the Tour de France, and has also had to work through some back luck, spending time out injured.

Liège-Bastogne-Liège has been his most successful Monument, with a third and fourth place to his name; his highest finish in Il Lombardia was 30th in 2023. Healy will be working alongside EF Education-EasyPost teammates Richard Carapaz and Alex Baudin.

Matteo Jorgenson (Visma-Lease a Bike)

Visma-Lease a Bike bring Matteo Jorgenson to Il Lombardia fresh off some decent results in the one-day races. He only has one Classic victory to his name from Dwars door Vlaanderen in 2023, however a spate of solid results has reiterated his competency over one-day hilly parcours and fast finishes with fifth place in the Giro dell’Emilia and a podium at Tre Valli Varesine.

That Giro dell’Emilia result was a brilliant team display, with Davide Piganzoli taking the victory and British rider Ben Tulett in fourth.

Christian Scaroni (XDS Astana)

Excellent in hilly one-day races, XDS Astana’s Christian Scaroni has been on fire in Italy as of late. Second at the GP Industria & Artigianato, third at the Giro della Toscana, fourth at Coppa Sabatini and seventh at Tre Valli Varesine, he is always one to watch out for and should place higher than his 15th in 2025.

He’s no doubt still riding high from his bronze medal in the European Championships road race too.

Other contenders to watch

This is the first race in 2026 that will see Primož Roglič and Evenepoel in the same Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe squad. Newly crowned European ITT Champion Roglič could an intriguing card to play with more eyes on the European Road Race Champion. Elsewhere, Oscar Onley just finished third at Giro dell’Emilia, and Michael Matthews has exploded into a run of good form. After sixth place in Quebec, he scored a silver medal at Worlds, though even with those climbing legs Lombardia should be a step too far. There’s also the Lotto Intermarché duo of Lennert van Eetvelt and Jarno Widar to look out for. Van Eetvelt recently claimed two stages and the overall at Tour de Slovaquie and rookie Widar impressively won Tre Valli Varesine in a sprint against Pidcock and Jorgenson.
